categories.name: Find Cameras in Your Area
categories.description: Databases and maps of ALPR camera deployments, sourced from public records and community reports.

items.name: FlockRadar
items.description: Open-source map of ALPR deployments. Every pin links to a public record (contract, council agenda, policy document).

items.name: UnFlocked
items.description: Crowdsourced ALPR camera locations mapped by state. Includes per-state camera counts and coverage estimates.

items.name: Eyes On Flock
items.description: Aggregates and analyzes data from Flock Safety's own public transparency portals. Tracks camera locations, search activity, and data-sharing practices.

items.name: Atlas of Surveillance (EFF)
items.description: Electronic Frontier Foundation database of surveillance technologies used by law enforcement, including ALPRs, drones, and body cameras.

items.name: Flock Camera Locations
items.description: Per-state maps with documented camera positions. Includes live data from community reports.

items.name: DeFlock
items.description: Crowdsourced camera sighting reports. Companion to the DeFlock mobile app for reporting camera locations.

categories.name: Public Records Law Guides
categories.description: State-by-state legal references for understanding your right to request government records.

items.name: RCFP Open Government Guide
items.description: Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press. Comprehensive state-by-state guide to public records and open meetings laws. The most thorough reference available.

items.name: NY Committee on Open Government
items.description: Official New York state resource for FOIL procedures, advisory opinions (25,000+ published), and compliance guidance.

items.name: FOIL It and Find Out
items.description: Practical New York FOIL guide with appeal templates, denial-handling strategies, and advice on finding contingency attorneys.

items.name: Sunlight in the City (NYC Comptroller)
items.description: NYC Comptroller's blueprint for FOIL operations. Useful for understanding how agencies are supposed to handle requests internally.

items.name: NFOIC State FOI Resources
items.description: National Freedom of Information Coalition. Links to state-level FOI coalitions and resources.

categories.name: Filing & Tracking Tools
categories.description: Platforms that help you submit, track, and publish public records requests.

items.name: MuckRock
items.description: File, track, and publish records requests. Handles submission, follow-ups, and appeals. Publicly archives results. Has an API for programmatic access.

items.name: FOIA.gov
items.description: Federal FOIA portal. For federal agency requests only (FBI, DHS, ICE, etc.). Not applicable to state/local requests.

categories.name: Advocacy & Legal Support
categories.description: Organizations working on surveillance oversight, privacy rights, and public records enforcement.

items.name: ACLU — Get the Flock Out
items.description: ACLU toolkit for communities opposing Flock camera deployments. Includes organizing guides, model legislation, and talking points.

items.name: Institute for Justice (IJ)
items.description: Public interest law firm. Currently recruiting plaintiffs for Fourth Amendment challenge to Westchester County's ALPR system. Represents clients free of charge.

items.name: NYCLU
items.description: New York Civil Liberties Union. Pursuing class action against Westchester County over ALPR privacy violations.

items.name: Electronic Frontier Foundation
items.description: EFF's street-level surveillance project. Research, advocacy, and legal analysis of ALPR, Flock, and related technologies.

items.name: Flip the Flock
items.description: State-by-state ALPR law summaries, advocacy resources, and community organizing guides.

items.name: Reporters Committee — Legal Hotline
items.description: Free legal assistance for journalists and citizens navigating public records denials.

categories.name: Background Reading
categories.description: Articles and investigations that provide context for ALPR surveillance and records request campaigns.

items.name: Cascadia Daily — Rodriguez Flock Campaign ($300K)
items.description: The article that started it all. How one person's 53 records requests to Washington municipalities led to $300K in settlements and 13 cancelled Flock contracts.

items.name: NYCLU — License Plate Readers Are Tracking New Yorkers
items.description: NYCLU analysis of how ALPR networks enable mass location tracking without warrants.

items.name: Flock Around and Find Out (Ritholtz)
items.description: Citizen's guide to local ALPR oversight. Overview of the surveillance landscape and community response.
